title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming
abstract: arXiv:2611.17395v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent advances in weight-space programming (WSP) have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can directly inspect and modify neural network weights without conventional gradient-based training. While this capability opens new possibilities for model improvement, it also raises an important security question: Can LLMs exploit weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks? To answer this question, we present an empirical security study of LLM-driven weight-space programming for backdoor injection. Specifically, we investigate whether general-purpose LLMs can directly modify the weights of target models according to natural-language instructions, without accessing task-specific data, performing forward passes, or computing gradients. translated_title: 大语言模型能编写后门吗？关于权重空间编程的实证安全研究
translated_abstract: 权重空间编程的最新进展表明，大语言模型（LLM）可以在不使用传统基于梯度训练的情况下，直接检查和修改神经网络的权重。虽然这一能力为模型改进开辟了新的可能性，但也引出了一个重要的安全问题：大语言模型能否利用权重空间编程向神经网络注入后门？为回答这一问题，我们对基于大语言模型的权重空间编程后门注入开展了一项实证安全研究。具体而言，我们研究通用大语言模型能否仅根据自然语言指令直接修改目标模型的权重，而无需访问任务特定数据、执行前向传播或计算梯度。我们评估了五个大语言模型作为权重编辑器，针对三种目标架构进行实验：MNIST 上的 MLP、CIFAR-10 上的 ResNet-18，以及 AG News 上的 Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct。我们的实验揭示了……
tldr: 本文通过实证安全研究首次系统评估了大语言模型在权重空间编程中的后门注入能力，表明通用大语言模型可以在不访问任务数据、不执行前向传播、不计算梯度的情况下，仅凭自然语言指令直接修改模型权重来注入后门，揭示了权重空间编程带来的新型安全威胁。
en_tdlr: This empirical security study shows that general-purpose LLMs can act as weight editors to inject backdoors into neural networks solely from natural-language instructions—without task-specific data, forward passes, or gradients—revealing a novel security threat posed by weight-space programming.
